1.א: §1—One who cooks on Shabbat when the pot needed one or two hours and he stirs the coals so it cooks sooner: Ritva Yevamot 18b s.v. “R. Huna said” suggests one might be liable—cooking adjacency is comparable to adjacency in Temple labor—see there.
1.ב: Same—§4 “forbidden to him forever”: see below §338.
1.ג: Magen Avraham §2: according to them it is davar sheyesh lo matirin—for even outside Jerusalem they would lack allowance without bitul, yet permitted outside Jerusalem (this implies unlike Tzitz Eliezer’s approach to treifah born on Yom Tov—Yom Tov issur might still not “nullify”). Rather: since outside-Jerusalem prohibition for kohanim is DSHLM, it does not nullify for zarim either; same for one who cooks on Shabbat—because for others the issur has matirin, it remains forbidden to the cook. Though terumah mixed for tamei kohen is DSHLM for zar’s tumah, zar’s prohibition is not DSHLM—and in truth even the zar is forbidden to eat it in tumah because this issur, having matirin for kohanim, does not nullify for the zar either.

2.ד: Same §4—perhaps discussing when it mixed; same if mixed on Shabbat—after Shabbat it is permitted; though on Shabbat bitul does not operate from DSHLM, bitul begins after Shabbat.

3.ה: §3—burying in sun derivatives—seems to me even bedieved forbidden as the sugya implies (“you thought the end supports the beginning…”); nonetheless perhaps after Shabbat permitted even for the cook himself—requires practical ruling.
3.ו: Magen Avraham §10—even during twilight; Rashba Ḥiddushim 20 permits insulating on chol bein ha-shmashot to warm in sun—anything heated erev Shabbat from sun fully cools Friday night and is not “mosif hevel”; chol itself adds heat (cf. §257 §3)—but that refers to boiling stew, not cold stew (see Ḥamimei Ḥayim ve-Kiriri Mekarer ch. 2).
3.ז: Same §4—and Yerushalmi agrees it is forbidden; Rashba Ḥiddushim cites Yerushalmi explicitly.
3.ח: Same §4—from erev permitted; Rashba writes one may leave on solar derivatives—no one is stringent about leaving on solar heat, and certainly for one who permits returning (food)—lean lenient; also seems logical that even fire derivatives may be left like a cleared stove since there is no fear of stoking.

4.ט: Magen Avraham §11—even placing on the kirah and placing stew erev while boiling before the Jew fires the kirah after cooling—perhaps permitted lechatchilah: “one supplies water / one supplies first fire” is rabbinic because then there would be Torah bishul; here when placing there is no bishul aḥar bishul and after cooling nothing happens—requires practical ruling.

5.י: §5—even third vessel; see Eishel Avraham this siman §134.
5.יא: Same Hagah—practice is to be careful lechatchilah; bedieved perhaps even keli rishon permitted since some permit entirely—Eishel Avraham §259 §111.

9.יב: Magen Avraham §31—no bishul aḥar bishul; so with ṣukar (sugar) permitted for that reason; also Responsa Pri Megadim and Mordekhai ve-Aggadah end—yet good to be stringent.

10.יג: §10—in Ahavat Olam kelal 41 §1: prohibition only pouring onto spices themselves; pouring beside them permitted. See Pri Megadim YD §95 Shakh §18.
10.יד: Magen Avraham §32—if poured, peel forbidden; whether peeling is “tikun”—see Eishel Avraham below §259 §111.

11.טו: Magen Avraham §35—seems to me forbidden; see Ḥovat Daat YD §91 Beurim §5.

12.טז: Magen Avraham §36—Maggid Mishneh seems to discuss even with pesik reisha; truly Maggid Mishneh wrote only regarding metal embers—where vessel repair doesn’t apply—joining doesn’t create liability; kettle repairs immediately when hardened—see Leḥem Mishneh; if pesik reisha clear, liable.

14.יז: §14—since it can cook there—even solar derivatives forbidden to soften where full cooking can occur—Ran explains sugya of “take second vessel and put” even at Tiberias hot springs (solar); Rashba Ḥiddushim too; Tosafot 48b s.v. “what’s different from kettle” seems to forbid lest one forget on fire but not solar—see analysis: Tosafot may follow Rashi “melting is cooking” so no melting in keli sheni to soften; Rashba explicitly permits softening in solar where it can cook; manuscript variants etc.—requires careful study.
